avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own means: money from the parks fund, equipment rental, blue-collar worker teams. Variances also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.titre: Contracts for planting on public land
etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and to Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved parks fund toward the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an extension at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the chalet at parc Pratt and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant planting, funded in part by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees there for planting.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026, at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the nursery in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, abrasive spreading, parking by-laws.
deneigement.enBref: This year, the City and its boroughs are signing, extending and paying for contracts related to snow: turnkey street snow removal, equipment rental with operators, vehicle towing and spring cleaning of streets and sidewalks. Some boroughs are drawing on their surpluses to cover winter expenses higher than expected. Others are amending their by-laws covering contractors who clear snow from private lots.

etapes.titre: Snow removal of downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie is hiring companies to maintain, clean and clear snow from Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six downtown public squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending by one year the snow removal of the Quartier des Spectacles, including abrasive spreading, snow loading and disposal.

Montréal-Nord is paying $106,150.97 more for the rental of a grader, and Saint-Léonard is allocating $200,000 from its surpluses to staff pay and the purchase of abrasives. Verdun is offering to have the city council itself provide staff for the snow disposal site during loading operations.

The city council, the executive committee and boroughs are extending by 6 or 12 months turnkey snow removal contracts in Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, as well as towing contracts, tractor-loader rentals and other equipment with operators. Ville-Marie is allocating $323,361.50 from its surpluses dedicated to snow removal to fund its share for 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal equipment rental services in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie start on November 1, 2026, and the extension runs until March 31, 2027.
The extended towing contracts start on November 15, 2026.
Montréal-Nord's towing contract covers services from November 15 to March 31 of each winter season.
The turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.
Saint-Léonard indicates that the adoption of its snow removal by-law is planned for September 8, 2026, with the coming into force announced for September 9, 2026.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law that raises the loan for the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 [CG26 0075]. The money must be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen production plant.

The agglomeration adds contingencies to the rehabilitation contract for the water pipe on rue de la Cathédrale, which leads to the McTavish reservoir, extends a leak detection contract on main pipes, and leases from Parcs Canada a 941 square metre piece of land under the canal de Lachine for maintaining two 600 mm pipes [CG26 0355]. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane sector.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer networks on October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, about six weeks each.
Rehabilitation of the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord and the bretelle Atwater to be finished by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
End of work on the rue de la Cathédrale water pipe postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant planned for 2029; contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 must end in the last quarter of 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump site, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on several fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel. It is requesting financial assistance from Québec for a footbridge and an east-west trail, approving a greenhouse complex led by the borough, and awarding contracts for electrical work at the environmental complex, park maintenance, and the redevelopment of rue De Louvain.

etapes.texte: The City is asking the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for assistance of up to $2,000,000 to build a footbridge and an east-west link in the park. The project includes a 900-metre trail, a footbridge about 150 metres long, and a 12.7-hectare meadow (CG26 0121).

etapes.titre: Green light for the greenhouse complex
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council approves the institutional and community greenhouse project, valued at $2,185,000 in construction costs, and assigns its delivery to the city council. The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of the project, and the city council accepts.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. the second phase of the electrical system upgrade work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, including a new power supply, a generator, and an automated system to manage biogas capture. It also awards two companies the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park, from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028 (CG26 0224).

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, walking corridors, bike facilities, and plantings.

The borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. the design, supply, and installation of the greenhouse complex, for $499,865.92 including taxes, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project includes two greenhouses with natural ventilation, interior partitions, and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouse installation work is scheduled to start in August 2026 and finish in December 2026.
The compost sifter rental covers the period from June 20 to October 15, 2026.
The call for projects under the TAPU program, for which the City is submitting its application, ends on November 26, 2026.
The greenhouses are expected to be put into service in winter 2027.
26 more hectares will be added to the park in 2027, in the Boisé Ouest sector.
The rue De Louvain construction project runs in three phases: May to November 2026, May to October 2027, and May to August 2028.

grand-parc-ouest.description: Canada's largest municipal park, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.
grand-parc-ouest.enBref: This year, the City is working on several sectors of the Grand parc de l'Ouest: repair of heritage walls and a culvert along chemin de Senneville, protection of natural environments, and routine maintenance of the grounds. It is also submitting the candidacy of the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for an international designation linked to the night sky.

etapes.titre: More money for the chemin de Senneville walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for the repair of the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. According to file 1255414002, buried stones, extra mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain these costs, and work resumes on May 15, 2026 to finish on July 10, 2026.

etapes.titre: Candidacy for the night sky at Cap-Saint-Jacques
etapes.texte: The City is submitting the candidacy of the 330-hectare Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the "Urban Night Sky Place" designation from DarkSky International. File 1250288001 provides for a lighting management plan, upgrading of light fixtures to standards, facilities for stargazing and astronomy programming.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité. The listing comes with conservation plans, and the 2025 report on surface areas is being filed.

The City is awarding a company the rebuilding of the culvert under chemin Senneville, for a total expenditure of $481,850.45, taxes included. The work includes repaving the roadway and replacing the guardrails, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub.

aSurveiller.texte: Filing of the lighting management plan for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector in February 2027.
Response from DarkSky International on the candidacy expected in April 2027.
Full compliance of the site's lighting in April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City is lending municipal buildings to organizations so they can open warming centres during the 2025-2026 winter. It is also funding community organizations working on homelessness, expanding to other boroughs a public works team managed by Ville-Marie, and setting up a framework for receiving private donations. Toward the end of the period, it purchases support services to help people move into housing near the encampments on rue Notre-Dame.

etapes.titre: Loans of buildings for warming centres
etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge to organizations that use them to shelter people experiencing homelessness: the former church at 5600, 12e Avenue in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est, and the former Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert. The loans run until April 30, 2026, and the City covers the energy and technical maintenance costs of the premises.

etapes.titre: Borough funding for warming centres and outreach
etapes.texte: Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers in municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville confirms a contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre, and Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for setting up the Bain Saint-Denis warming centre.

City council adopts a mechanism governing private cash donations for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects: donors do not choose which project is funded, and the City may refuse a donation. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on rent support.

The City grants $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the encampments on rue Notre-Dame move toward shelter and housing, from July 13 to October 18, 2026. It pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the Nuit des sans-abri, and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026 ruling on the encampments under the viaduc Van Horne.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate near the encampments on rue Notre-Dame ends on October 18, 2026.
The public works team agreement with Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.
Support for the Nuit des sans-abri covers the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions.

logement.description: Grants, land and social, affordable or student housing projects, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: This year, the City approves the 2026 budgets of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal (OMHM), transfers or buys land intended for social housing, and provides grants to organizations and co-ops that build housing. It also amends the by-law requiring developers to include social and affordable housing in their projects.

etapes.texte: City council approves the 2026 budget of the SHDM, which manages 393 buildings and more than 5,200 affordable housing units, and that of the OMHM. The urban agglomeration council also approves the OMHM's 2026 budget, which houses 42,587 households and goes from $541M in 2025 to $605.6M in 2026.

The City accepts from the Government of Canada half of the rights to a 3,658.8 square metre piece of land on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, at no cost. It also transfers free of charge to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni a 789.6 square metre piece of land at 7965, boulevard de l'Acadie, with a $110,000 devaluation for 2026.

etapes.titre: Rehousing assistance and easing of the by-law
etapes.texte: The City signs two 2025-2026 funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary housing and housing search assistance, including $500,000 for the OMHM's service. It then adopts an amendment to the Règlement visant à améliorer l'offre en matière de logement social, abordable et familial, following a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026.

The City adds $877,312 to its assistance for Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project, consisting of 26 new units, from the by-law's social component fund.

aSurveiller.texte: Occupancy of the 350 units at Technopôle Angus expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest.
SHDM's 72-unit building on 2e Avenue: construction to start by the end of 2026 and delivery in May 2028.
Projects announced by the SHDM: De Maisonneuve in spring 2026, Jardin des Prairies and Gilford in fall 2026.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: The City amended two leases to continue renting out parts of a lot south of rue de Louvain, west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. One is used as a parking lot for Société de transport de Montréal agents' vehicles, for a total rent of $49,293 [CM26 0078], the other as pay parking by mobile app.

etapes.titre: Contract for the redevelopment of rue De Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included. The work involves sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: Land lent for agriculture and programming
etapes.texte: The City extended the free loan of land to organizations: a 10,000-square-foot community garden, and two parts of a lot for sunflowers and a greenhouse, a property subsidy valued at $247,009 [CM26 0698]. The borough also paid $35,000 for the Esplanade-Louvain pop-up space, authorized an event-based and temporary use on a vacant lot, and asked city council to prepare a programming lease on a 78,244-square-foot lot.

The borough adopted a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, followed by the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It also launched an amendment to its urban planning by-law to increase the height and density permitted at the corner of avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal starts on October 1, 2026, for three years.
The land loan for the sunflowers and greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The rue De Louvain construction site takes place in three phases: from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the end of the development work, expected around 2032.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: This year, the City is preparing the ground, both literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack. It obtained more time from the Québec government to sell a first piece of land, guaranteed a loan for studies, and adopted two loan by-laws for streets, sewers and waterworks in the sector. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City an extension until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, located west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. According to the file, the postponement does not involve any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 deed of transfer remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to the organization GALOPH that will be used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and asset management in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build main water pipes between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Project for four buildings on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which is to house a municipal sports and leisure centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector, and a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: The sale of a first piece of land must be completed no later than October 31, 2027.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transition nursery).

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: This year, the City is awarding contracts to redo parks in several boroughs: play areas, water play areas, sports fields, trails and plantings. It is also adjusting contracts already underway and paying for land decontamination work. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is funding work on the chemin de Senneville, submitting an application for an international dark sky designation, and entrusting the maintenance of certain sectors.

etapes.texte: The City is entrusting the winning team of an architecture competition with the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, for a total expenditure of $10,559,257.81, taxes included. It is also paying $174,471.56 to the arrondissement of Verdun for soil and environmental studies at the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract to repair the heritage walls on the chemin de Senneville. It is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and is registering the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, in the registry of protected natural areas.

The City is adding $153,434.14 to the contract for site supervision at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois, where work is continuing until June 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is moving amounts between contingencies and incidentals for the parc des Hirondelles and parc du Sault-au-Récollet, and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension is adding contingencies to the parc Villeray site.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on the parc Denise-Morelle is to begin in early August 2026 and end in November 2026.
The borough is aiming for adoption at the executive committee on October 7, 2026 and at city council on October 19, 2026 for the lane strip at the parc Le Prévost.
For the artwork at the parc des Eaux-Cachées: winner selection in October 2026, contract in December 2026, and installation in 2028.
The response from DarkSky International is expected in April 2027; the lighting plan must be submitted in February 2027 and the site brought into compliance by April 2032.
Final acceptance of the work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois is expected in June 2027.
Work on the parc J.O.R.-Leduc is to be completed in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares. They are adopting funding rules, paying money to business development corporations, then issuing the ordinances that close streets to cars and regulate sales, noise and occupation of the roadway. At the end of the season, reopening schedules are adjusted and two files concern the status and name of public squares.

etapes.titre: Settlement of a dispute over a public square
etapes.texte: The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough settles out of court, for $41,686.46, a lawsuit related to the development work on the public square at the corner of rues Beaubien Est and Boyer. The settlement is concluded without admission of liability.

etapes.titre: Rules and money for the 2026 season
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that sets the conditions for grants to its business development corporations for pedestrianizing streets, with applications due no later than February 16, 2026. The executive committee then authorizes transfers of $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries.

The boroughs pay out sums to business development corporations and their projects: $102,045 for rue Villeray, $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe. Outremont allocates $105,000, net of taxes, to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awards a contract of $287,724.94, taxes included, to transport people with reduced mobility and seniors on demand on avenue du Mont-Royal, and bans amplified instruments on its pedestrian streets. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve temporarily removes 113 paid parking spaces, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on a closed street on avenue de Monkland, and the City pays $40,000 to animate the rue Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street.

etapes.titre: Status, name and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes a 899-square-metre lot, at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier, from street (public square) status to local park status, and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite". Le Plateau-Mont-Royal divides avenue du Mont-Royal into three sections with separate reopening dates.

aSurveiller.texte: Reopening of avenue du Mont-Royal: between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Full reopening of avenue Bernard to traffic as of September 25, 2026.
The pedestrian streets and public squares of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (avenue Royal, avenue Madison, Placette CDN) remain closed to cars until October 31, 2026.
Boroughs' accountability reporting in November 2026 and return of unspent funds in December 2026.
The on-demand transport contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period until December 31, 2027; the contribution for avenue Lacombe runs until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special project, and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, following public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of heritage-interest buildings, regulates lodging and service establishments for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects, and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public assembly took place on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation ran from March 11 to March 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses, and site coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenues Papineau, Émile-Journault and André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevards Crémazie and Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville asks for twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève asks for six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory, and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, certificates of authorization, and cadastral operations. Following the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the plans for view corridors and heights; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain works in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal subject to approval.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, following a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève states it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027, as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027, to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood stations, council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is funding and equipping the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal (SPVM): a loan for specialized equipment, purchases of vehicles, ammunition and a boat, maintenance contracts and lease renewals for neighbourhood stations. It is also accepting grants from Québec and Ottawa for specialized teams, and lending officers to the RCMP and the Sûreté du Québec. After the June 22, 2026 shooting in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, several borough councils adopted motions of support for the SPVM.

etapes.texte: The City is purchasing 11 motorcycles for road patrol, 2 pickup trucks for the mounted unit, and a patrol boat with its trailer for the port sector [CG26 0141, CE26 1145, CG26 0441]. It is also entering into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition for police firearms training [CG26 0316].

The City is extending housekeeping services at headquarters, mail courier services, and maintenance of the call dispatch system software [CG26 0149, CG26 0318, CG26 0248]. It is also awarding new contracts for meals for detained persons and for carpentry and painting services in SPVM buildings [CG26 0218, CE26 0910, CE26 1015].

aSurveiller.texte: The « Fèves au lard » day organized by the Fraternité des policiers et policières at neighbourhood station 46 is held on October 23, 2026; Anjou has bought 62 tickets.
The lease for the metro unit space at neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins on February 1, 2027.
The patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
Work to replace the oil heating system in the mounted unit building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides about the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.
transport-collectif.enBref: This year, the City approves the Société de transport de Montréal's budget and borrowings, sells or lends land to the STM for its stations and equipment, and oversees metro construction sites. It also signs agreements to have municipal work carried out at the same time as work on the Blue Line extension.

etapes.titre: Work related to stations and bus stops
etapes.texte: The City entrusts the STM with carrying out its own municipal work at the future Pie-IX and Viau stations, on rue Jean-Talon Est, and authorizes spending of $3,808,451.29 (CG26 0175). It signs an agreement with the STM to build a pavilion attached to the Wiseman ventilation building, in Outremont, and Ahuntsic-Cartierville modifies its bus waiting areas as part of the network overhaul.

The City buys advertising space in the metro and buses for Espace pour la vie, for a maximum of $172,462.50 (CG26 0164). Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce signs a new access agreement for an STM site on boulevard Décarie, and Ville-Marie authorizes the STM to work day and night in the Green Line tunnel, between Berri-UQAM and Saint-Laurent, from June 10 to July 31, 2026.

Elected officials approve several STM loan by-laws and the corresponding changes to the capital works program: reserved lanes and priority traffic lights for buses, repair of metro infrastructure and surface buildings, cybersecurity, extending the service life of the MR-73 cars and starting their replacement.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the STM employee parking lot, in Ahuntsic-Cartierville, runs for three years starting October 1, 2026, for 92 days per year.
Work at the Rielle ventilation building, in Verdun, is expected to continue until December 2027.
Rue Wilderton will be closed for a maximum of two weeks during the 2027 summer holidays, for the reconstruction of the tunnel bridge; the work is planned from June 2026 to March 2028.
According to the Blue Line extension file, contracts are awarded in August and October 2026, integrated municipal work takes place in 2028-2029, and the stations are expected to open in 2031.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the bike-sharing system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes and parts for the BIXI system, repairing existing bike lanes, and regularizing land it rents from Hydro-Québec for bike paths. Boroughs are managing traffic around bike lanes, cleaning the network, and having BIXI stations installed during street work. The City is also asking the Québec government for money to build new bike lanes.

etapes.texte: City council awards a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for BIXI bikes, stations and docking points, as the supplier holds the patents for the system. It also adds $3,400,000 to the contract of Bruneau Électrique inc. for the sustainable mobility corridors on rues Hochelaga and du Havre, bringing this contract to $11,399,999.99.

The City pays $125,167.62 to Hydro-Québec for rent from 2014 to 2025 on land occupied by bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then signs a 10-year lease, worth $46,896, for a strip of about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles where a bike path runs.

etapes.titre: Cleaning and repair of bike paths
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the spring cleaning of narrow bike paths, for $153,395.05 over thirty-six months. City council approves Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike path work, including the repair of the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie and that of the bike path on rue De Louvain; Outremont files a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie into a one-way bike path.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awards Cojalac inc. a $1,428,909.30 contract that includes installing a BIXI station at the intersection of Parthenais and Gauthier, and the Sud-Ouest retains Groupe Damex inc. for three green alleys and the electrical supply for a BIXI station. The executive committee awards $394,851.17 to Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for the steel bases of the stations.
The executive committee recommends submitting four funding requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for bike paths on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier.

aSurveiller.texte: REV Lajeunesse work, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie: call for tenders in May 2026, contracts awarded in June, work from July to August 2026.
Hochelaga and du Havre streets worksite: resumes in spring 2026 and delivery in spring or summer 2026.
UCI Road World Championships in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; roadway work is planned on sections of the route in Ville-Marie.
Repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, for $570,000 in 2027.
Lease with Hydro-Québec in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles in effect until December 31, 2035.
